consensus_summary: Consensus primary meaning is divine wrath and eschatological judgment: grapes crushed underfoot picture God/Messiah trampling the wicked with blood flowing as wine (Isa 63; Joel 3; Rev 14/19; Lam 1). Abundance/blessing (overflowing presses) and vineyard-parable furniture are recognized but secondary or context-specific alternatives; Christological passion readings also appear.
book_summary: Winepress as the vineyard’s reckoning where a people’s fruit is pressed and rendered to the Owner in one of two vintages: presses bursting with new wine for good grapes, or the growers themselves trodden in “the great winepress of the wrath of God” (blood for wine) when the vintage is wickedness.
consensus_core_identification: Primary symbol of God’s wrathful judgment via trampling the wicked
book_core_identification: Dual reckoning of vineyard fruit rendered to the Owner (blessing or wrathful treading according to fruit quality)
boundary_disagreement: Consensus isolates judgment as the dominant independent symbolic use and treats abundance as a separate secondary sense; the book unifies both as co-equal alternative outcomes of a single Owner-reckoning process tied to Isa 5 / vineyard-parable fruit evaluation, elevating the blessing texts into the core.
material_contradiction: None; the book retains the wrath/judgment sense as one of the two vintages without denying or replacing it.
rationale: Minimum cores overlap on the shared judgment imagery and key texts (Joel 3, Isa 63, Rev 14, Lam 1) plus the abundance texts, so the central referents are not replaced. The book nevertheless materially re-frames and broadens the extension by synthesizing the two uses under “vineyard’s reckoning” (explicitly linking Isa 5:2,7 and the parables), making abundance co-primary rather than secondary and conditioning both outcomes on the quality of the people’s fruit. This is a genuine change of boundary and precision, hence REFINED rather than MATCH or DIVERGENT.
strongest_objection: The dual-reckoning synthesis may over-unify what the consensus treats as distinct primary (judgment) versus secondary (abundance) or incidental (vineyard furniture) senses, and it omits the common Christological/passion reading of the lone treader.
